clue.text: Obviously a lot below standard

parts.note: the phrase for something poor is read as a plain statement that it falls short of 'a lot'

explanation.surface: A remark that something is clearly well short of the required level.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom for 'mediocre' is read literally: whatever falls short of 'much' plainly falls short of a lot.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for poor quality, saying something barely reaches any decent level.

clue.text: One of two openings under the bridge

definitions.text: One of two openings under the bridge

parts.words: One of two openings under the bridge
parts.note: the bridge is the bony ridge of the face, not a river crossing, and the pair of openings sit beneath it

explanation.surface: A description of arches beneath a river crossing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bridge' suggests a river span with arches; it is the bridge of the nose.
explanation.definitionFit: Each of the pair of air passages in the face opens just below the bony ridge of the nose.

clue.text: Aide-memoire such as a diary

parts.note: a diary prompts its owner about appointments when they fall due, so it is a prompt that arrives at the right moment

explanation.surface: A diary described as a memory aid.
explanation.definitionFit: A prompt arriving at the right moment is exactly what an aide-memoire such as a diary provides.

clue.text: Water game

definitions.meaning: a small body of still water, such as a pond
a cue sport played on a table with pockets

explanation.surface: Water polo or a similar game.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a pond-like stretch of water and a pocket billiards game played with cues.

clue.text: Not in a tedious way

annotationWithheld.why: Not in a tedious way (7) for OUTSIDE: 'Not in' gives the definition, but nothing in 'a tedious way' yields OUT or SIDE; likely a misread clue.

clue.text: See 1
Eminent conductor, maybe, at Rome's disposal

indicators.note: disposal here is arrangement or setting out, so the letters before it are laid out afresh

explanation.surface: A great conductor available to serve the city of Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disposal' means arrangement: the letters of AT ROMES are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A distinguished musician, especially a famous orchestral leader, is honoured with this Italian title.

clue.text: Prompted to play snooker?

definitions.meaning: given a signal to speak or act, as an actor is
struck the ball with the long stick used in snooker

explanation.surface: Someone was urged to take up snooker.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor given a signal and a player striking a ball with a stick share the same past-tense verb.

clue.text: Makes one slip in a letter to the Greeks

indicators.note: makes is read as 'makes into', so the following words are reworked into something new

explanation.surface: Someone commits an error while writing to Greek people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Makes' signals the anagram of ONE SLIP; 'a letter to the Greeks' is a character of their alphabet, not correspondence.
explanation.definitionFit: The fifth character of the Greek alphabet, a short E.

clue.text: A fortune from textiles, perhaps

parts.note: a riches gained from fabrics would literally be cloth riches; the phrase usually means worldly possessions

explanation.surface: A mill owner getting rich from cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Worldly riches and possessions, read literally as riches made of fabric.

clue.text: From Sophie Tucker's old song we hear it would be 31 for December

indicators.note: we hear tells the solver the phrase is spoken and matched by sound to a differently spelt one

parts.note: December has thirty-one days, so adding up those days gives 31

explanation.surface: A trivia note about a famous Sophie Tucker song and the calendar.
explanation.walkthrough: The total ('sum') of December's days is 31, and 'sum of these days' sounds like the song title. Sophie Tucker was an American vaudeville singer.
explanation.definitionFit: Sophie Tucker's signature tune, the early twentieth-century hit she recorded and sang for decades.

clue.text: Part of the Tyrolean scene

indicators.note: the answer is taken out of the following words, being part of them

explanation.surface: Something forming a piece of an Alpine view.
explanation.definitionFit: A character played by an actor is a part in a play or film.

clue.text: Same again for a single non drinker in the party

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another

parts.note: a do is an informal word for a party
I is the Roman numeral one
TT means teetotal, someone who drinks no alcohol

explanation.surface: A request for another round, with one abstainer at the party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' signals the container; 'non drinker' is the teetotaller convention and 'single' the Roman one.
explanation.definitionFit: The word used to repeat what was just said, meaning likewise or the same.

clue.text: Small change found on fish skin

parts.note: P stands for penny, the smallest coin
an eel is a long snake-like fish

explanation.surface: A coin discovered on a fish's skin.
explanation.definitionFit: The outer layer of a fruit, such as an orange or banana.

clue.text: It's betwixt and between red and green, by the way

definitions.text: It's betwixt and between red and green, by the way

parts.words: It's betwixt and between red and green, by the way
parts.note: 'by the way' means at the roadside, where traffic signals show a colour between stop and go

explanation.surface: An aside about an in-between colour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by the way' looks like an aside, but means at the side of the road.
explanation.definitionFit: The traffic signal shown between stop and go on British roads.

clue.text: See 13
The French butter that is located in Wyoming

parts.note: la is the French feminine word for 'the'
a ram butts with its head, so it is a butter
i.e. abbreviates id est, Latin for 'that is'

explanation.surface: French butter turns up in a western US state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'butter' is one who butts, a ram, not the dairy spread.
explanation.definitionFit: A city in the US state of Wyoming, known from Western films and television.

clue.text: No point taking a shot in the dark

definitions.text: taking a shot in the dark
definitions.meaning: firing without a target, so without direction

explanation.surface: It is pointless to fire when you cannot see.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking purpose, and literally firing with no target in view.

clue.text: Such an award can be withering

parts.note: a trophy is a cup or prize given to a winner

explanation.surface: A remark that some prizes can be cutting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'withering' looks like scorn but is wasting away.
explanation.definitionFit: Wasting away of a body part or tissue through disuse or disease, like a plant drying up.

clue.text: Ticking off the French in smart surroundings

indicators.note: surroundings means one piece encloses another

parts.note: to smart is to sting with pain
la is the French feminine word for 'the'

explanation.surface: Telling off the French in a fashionable setting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surroundings' signals the container; 'smart' is the verb for a stinging pain, not the adjective for stylish.
explanation.definitionFit: Harsh criticism or a scolding, a reprimand.

clue.text: Work hard on Charles Lamb finding a Shakespeare character

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard
Elia was the pen name of the essayist Charles Lamb

explanation.surface: Studying the essayist Charles Lamb to find a Shakespeare role.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' joins the pieces in order; Charles Lamb wrote his Essays of Elia under that pen name.
explanation.definitionFit: The young woman in Hamlet who drowns herself.

clue.text: Examining pupils is part of his work

definitions.text: Examining pupils is part of his work

parts.words: Examining pupils is part of his work
parts.note: the pupils are those of the eye, not schoolchildren, so this is an eye doctor, not a school inspector

explanation.surface: A school inspector's job description.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pupils' suggests a schoolroom; they are the openings at the centre of the eye.
explanation.definitionFit: An eye specialist, whose job includes looking into the dark centres of the eyes.

clue.text: Painkiller a number deny when confused

indicators.note: confused means the letters of the next word are jumbled

explanation.surface: A painkiller that several people mistakenly refuse.
explanation.definitionFit: A medicine that relieves pain, an analgesic.

clue.text: Cover synonymous with 12

definitions.meaning: an outer skin or crust covering fruit or cheese
12 across is the word for fruit skin, meaning the same

explanation.surface: A covering that means the same as another entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A tough outer skin on fruit or cheese, the same as the earlier skin entry.

clue.text: Indefinite number with the shivers

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral five
ague is a fever with shivering fits

explanation.surface: An uncertain count of people with chills.
explanation.definitionFit: Unclear or imprecise, not definite.

clue.text: Hit back in Nevada

indicators.note: back means the word for hit is read backwards

parts.note: a oner is a heavy blow

explanation.surface: Striking back somewhere in Nevada.
explanation.definitionFit: A city in Nevada famous for gambling and quick divorces.

clue.text: Defeat with a blunt sword

definitions.meaning: a light fencing weapon with a button on its point

explanation.surface: Beating someone with a blunted weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: To thwart a plan, and also a light fencing weapon with a buttoned tip.

annotationWithheld.why: Loosen up in round one (4) for UNDO: 'Loosen' may define, but no reading of 'up in round one' yields the letters; likely a misread clue.

clue.text: How we're taught to never end a sentence with

definitions.text: How we're taught to never end a sentence with

parts.words: How we're taught to never end a sentence with
parts.note: the old grammar rule bans ending on a small linking word such as 'with', and the clue itself ends on one

explanation.surface: A grammar rule about sentence endings, which the clue itself breaks.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue breaks the rule it describes by ending on 'with', and splits an infinitive too.
explanation.definitionFit: In the manner of a word such as 'with' or 'to', the kind of word grammar rules say should never close a sentence.

clue.text: Clobber a garden pest

definitions.meaning: a shell-less slimy creature that eats plants

explanation.surface: Hitting a garden pest.
explanation.definitionFit: To hit hard, and a shell-less mollusc that eats garden plants.

clue.text: Metrical foot to cheer about

indicators.note: about means the letters of the preceding words are turned around and rearranged

explanation.surface: A rhythm in verse that is something to celebrate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' signals the anagram of TO CHEER.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit of verse rhythm with one stressed then one unstressed syllable.
